evidence: LoadBoard (repo_postgres.go:91-102) SELECTs FROM board_cells LEFT JOIN board_cell_tracks LEFT JOIN tracks WHERE bc.session_id=$1 — the 0001_init.sql tables. grep 'INSERT INTO board_cells|board_cell_tracks|INSERT INTO tracks' over server/ = ZERO hits: nothing ever writes those tables. The builder/curation path writes only the 0002_boards.sql tables (admin_store.go:90 INSERT INTO board_tracks, :171 board_layout_cells, :204 board_layout_cell_tracks) keyed by board_id, and AttachBoard (admin_store.go:383-385) only does UPDATE game_sessions SET board_id. engine.Run (engine.go:210-215) calls repo.LoadBoard(cfg.SessionID) on boot and only sets e.board if err==nil && b!=nil; since board_cells is empty, LoadBoard returns the 'no board for session' error (repo_postgres.go:155) and e.board stays nil. LoadBoard NEVER joins game_sessions.board_id, so the persisted board_id is ignored on restart. The board_id->0002-tables loader (LoadBoardByID, admin_store.go:301) exists but is invoked ONLY from the live attachBoard HTTP handler (layout.go:198->engine.ReloadBoard:204), never on boot. Mitigation: (a) sample board is injected only when Postgres is UNAVAILABLE (main.go:65,116 needSampleBoard on mem-repo path), not on the Postgres path; (b) an admin must manually re-attach via the Board Builder after every restart (main.go:59 log even hints at this). So a Postgres-backed server silently boots boardless on every restart until a human re-attaches.
fix: On boot, resolve the board through the persisted link instead of the dead 0001 tables: add a repo method to read game_sessions.board_id and, if set, load via the existing LoadBoardByID (0002 tables); wire engine.Run (or main.go) to call it so e.board is restored. Minimal version: change LoadBoard's query to join game_sessions.board_id -> board_layout_cells/board_layout_cell_tracks/board_tracks (mirroring LoadBoardByID) keyed by session_id.
